Testing seams, refactoring, and interview-safe cleanup

Use tests and small refactors to prove design quality while preserving momentum during a live round.

20-30 min LLD flow Machine coding, testing, and follow-up handling 4 guided stops

Why this lesson matters

Interviewers often evaluate whether you can recognize design pressure early and carve out seams before the implementation hardens into messy code.

Start with this framing

Interview framing

Interviewers often evaluate whether you can recognize design pressure early and carve out seams before the implementation hardens into messy code.

What to say first

  • Expose seams around external dependencies.

    Show likely answer
    • Expose seams around external dependencies.
    • Interviewers often evaluate whether you can recognize design pressure early and carve out seams before the implementation hardens into messy code.
    • Inject collaborators with external effects so business rules can be tested with simple fakes, and keep deterministic logic easy to exercise.

  • Test the rules that protect important invariants.

    Show likely answer
    • Test the rules that protect important invariants.
    • Inject collaborators with external effects so business rules can be tested with simple fakes, and keep deterministic logic easy to exercise.
    • If a method grows too broad, extract the policy or helper that carries the real decision-making rather than scattering utility classes everywhere.

  • Refactor only after the behavior is visible and working.

    Show likely answer
    • Refactor only after the behavior is visible and working.
    • Refactor after a working slice, not before
    • Mention the next refactor you would make after the interview

Common pitfalls

What to avoid

  • Writing no tests or examples for critical rules when the prompt invites it.
  • Refactoring repeatedly without improving the design story.
  • Optimizing code style before the main behavior is correct.
